pages.summary: Hero wastes the fold on a 28-word meta-sentence and 5 large stat tiles. Zero content cards visible above the fold at 1440x900. Signal-to-noise in hero ~35%.

scores.visual_breathing_room: excessive vertical padding (48px top) pushes content down
scores.action_clarity: 6 nav pills + 4 numbered journey cards = 10 competing CTAs

issues.problem: 28-word provenance sentence ('54 mental models, 161 patterns, 9 anti-patterns extracted from 880 entities across 34 Azure Well-Architected Framework documents using LightRAG + Claude Opus 4.6') is the first body text — it repeats the stat tiles directly below and ends with tool names that are noise for readers.
issues.fix: Replace with a 10-word promise: 'Mission-critical Azure patterns, one card each — scan, then drill.' Move provenance to a collapsed <details> at page bottom.

issues.problem: 5 stat tiles (54/161/168/980/9) consume ~120px of prime fold space but are already stated in the subtitle. Duplicate information, zero new insight.
issues.fix: Either delete the stats block OR delete the subtitle. Keep one. If keeping stats, shrink .stat .n from default large size to 28px and put them on a single inline row under the h1.

issues.problem: padding:48px 20px 32px + h1 + subtitle + stats + nav = ~560px of fold used before any content. At 1440x900, 0 model cards are visible.
issues.fix: Cut .hero padding to 20px 20px 16px. Merge .nav into the same row as the h1 on desktop (flex space-between). Target: first model card visible by 700px scroll position.

issues.problem: 6 emoji-prefixed pills compete for attention with the 4 numbered journey cards immediately below. Two overlapping navigation systems == decision paralysis (high ADHD cost).
issues.fix: Delete .nav. The #journey section IS the navigation. Add a sticky, minimal top bar only with: [Cards] [Anti-patterns] [Graph].

issues.problem: Each card has 18-25 words of explanation; 4 cards × full-width = another ~400px of meta-content before the user reaches real models. 'Follow this path from big picture to deep detail. Each step links to the next.' is pure instruction-about-instruction.
issues.fix: Collapse to a single 1-line breadcrumb: 'Graph → Cards → Trees → Anti-patterns'. Delete the intro sentence. Each word is clickable.

issues.problem: Page is 7240 words on one scroll. No progressive disclosure. ADHD readers will bounce; autistic readers will get lost without section landmarks.
issues.fix: Introduce 5 top-level tabs (Models / Patterns / Services / Anti-patterns / Graph). Render only the active tab. Persist tab in URL hash.

issues.problem: minmax(480px, 1fr) forces very wide cards; on 1440 viewport only 2 columns fit, leaving long reading lines (>90ch) in card bodies.
issues.fix: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(340px, 1fr)); so 3–4 columns fit at desktop and line length stays ~55–70ch.

issues.problem: Dense paragraphs in .mantra + when/without/tradeoff without visual separation between sections beyond 12px margin. High cognitive load for a neurodivergent reader scanning.
issues.fix: Add a 1px dotted separator between card-sections and render 'WHEN / WITHOUT / TRADEOFF' labels as sticky left-column micro-headings (flex-row with 80px label column).

issues.problem: Italic + 15px + low-contrast #e6edf3 on dark is the least-readable element on the page; it is also the first thing the eye lands on inside a card.
issues.fix: Change to non-italic, 16px, color:#fff, font-weight:500. Remove quotes; use a left accent border (3px solid var(--accent)) instead.

pages.summary: Radial tree is clear and beautiful. Sidebar crams 133 words at 13px with tight 1.5 line-height — a micro wall-of-text in a narrow column.

scores.signal_to_noise: 75% (sidebar is all content, but too compressed)
scores.visual_breathing_room: sidebar is cramped; graph canvas is great
scores.action_clarity: 'Expand all / Collapse / Reset' unclear before first interaction

issues.problem: 133 words at 13px / line-height 1.5 in a ~360px column. No separators between the 4 sections beyond uppercase micro-labels. Reader must parse dense nested information.
issues.fix: Bump .sidebar ul to font-size:14px, line-height:1.7. Add 12px top-margin + 1px divider between each h2 block.

issues.problem: 52-word definition paragraph ('A security model that limits network traffic... centered on eliminating trust and enforcing verification.') — the LAST item in the sidebar and the longest. Buried where it should be promoted.
issues.fix: Move the one-sentence first clause ('A security model that limits network traffic between workloads based on strict access policies.') up to replace the italic mantra. Keep the rest collapsed behind 'more →'.

issues.problem: 11px uppercase with 1px letter-spacing is below the WCAG-recommended minimum for body-adjacent labels. Dyslexic/low-vision users struggle.
issues.fix: font-size:12px, letter-spacing:0.5px, color: var(--text) not --text-dim. Keep uppercase; raise contrast.

issues.problem: Each bullet runs 10–15 words. 'Overly permissive network policies persist undetected without continuous verification' is 8 words before the verb. Passive voice, Azure product-dense.
issues.fix: Enforce ≤10 words per bullet in source data. Lead with the concrete verb+noun: 'Lateral movement after one breach (flat network)'. Edit cards.json, not CSS.

issues.problem: 4 buttons with symbol-only icons on first load. 'Expand all' is ambiguous — expand what? No hover tooltip observed.
issues.fix: Add title attributes. Replace ⤢/⤡ with text 'Expand +' / 'Collapse −'. Put '← Back to cards' on the left; action buttons on the right with 16px gap.

issues.problem: Orange warning-colored block (#3d2a14 + #f59e0b border) used for a neutral 'tradeoff' note. Color semantics conflict with actual warnings (anti-patterns). Autistic readers rely on consistent color semantics.
issues.fix: Use a neutral cyan/slate accent for tradeoffs. Reserve orange/red strictly for anti-patterns and failures.

issues.problem: Radial labels rotate along the spoke; at certain angles they read upside-down or tangent to the page, forcing head-tilt. Accessibility hostile.
issues.fix: Flip labels whose angle > 90° or < -90° so text always reads left-to-right (mirror the transform). D3: `d.angle > Math.PI/2 && d.angle < 3*Math.PI/2 ? rotate(180) translate(-r,0) : rotate(0) translate(r,0)`.

pages.summary: The graph is the feature, but the first render is a hairball with overlapping labels and 17 live controls. Zero onboarding; users do not know what to click first.

scores.visual_breathing_room: none — nodes/labels collide in center mass
scores.action_clarity: low — 12 toggle checkboxes + slider + search + 2 buttons, no primary CTA

issues.problem: 271 nodes and 1969 edges render at once with labels always on. Text overlaps ~40 times in the central cluster; the user cannot read anything without first disabling labels or zooming in.
issues.fix: On load, default 'show labels' OFF. Auto-zoom to the top-10 mental-model nodes only. Fade Document/Section nodes to 30% opacity until user toggles them.

issues.problem: No hint of what to do. 'Click a node to inspect.' is 4 words in low-contrast text halfway down the sidebar. ADHD/autistic users freeze when no single next step is obvious.
issues.fix: Add a prominent first-run callout at top of sidebar: '▶ Start here: click any large orange dot.' Dismiss on first click. Persist dismissal in localStorage.

issues.element: SHOW NODE TYPES (7 checkboxes) + SHOW EDGE TYPES (4 checkboxes)
issues.problem: 12 toggles all enabled by default = cognitive overload. User must understand 'Section (H2)' vs 'Subsection (H3)' vs 'Product' vs 'Pattern' before anything is useful.
issues.fix: Collapse behind a single 'Filters' <details> closed by default. Provide 3 preset chips instead: [Concepts only] [Concepts + Patterns] [Everything]. Advanced toggles stay behind the fold.

issues.problem: 8-item legend duplicates the 7 node-type checkboxes on the left. Same information twice, split across the viewport — forces saccades.
issues.fix: Delete the top-right legend. Show color dots inside each checkbox label on the left (already partially done — commit fully and remove the duplicate).

issues.problem: Slider with no tick marks, no max label, and no live count of how many nodes remain after filtering. Users don't know the effect.
issues.fix: Show 'MIN MENTIONS: 1  (271 of 271 nodes)'. Update count on input. Add marks at 1/2/5/10.

issues.problem: Labels rendered as straight text in SVG with no collision avoidance and no halo. Dark background + white text + overlapping labels = multiple words illegible (e.g. 'Design recommendations' repeated 8+ times stacking).
issues.fix: Add a 2px dark stroke (paint-order:stroke) behind label text. Cull labels that would overlap using a simple quadtree collision pass each tick; re-show on hover.

issues.problem: Placeholder 'Filter nodes by label…' but pressing Enter or typing does not visibly reduce the graph until exact substring match; no fuzzy match, no result count.
issues.fix: Debounce 150ms, dim non-matching nodes to 10% opacity instead of hiding, and show 'N matches' next to the input.

global_issues.problem: Body copy at 13px across sidebar and card meta. Below the 14–16px floor recommended for ADHD/dyslexic readers.
global_issues.fix: Set :root { --fs-body: 15px; --fs-small: 13px; --fs-micro: 12px; } and replace every 13px literal with var(--fs-body).

global_issues.problem: Multiple containers (guide, model-card body, cards-grid at 480px minmax) yield reading lines >85 characters. Optimal is 55–70ch.
global_issues.fix: Apply max-width: 66ch on .card-body p, .guide p, .detail-card p. Use ch units so the limit tracks font-size.

global_issues.problem: Orange/amber is used for both 'tradeoff' (neutral info) and 'anti-pattern' (warning). This breaks semantic consistency, which autistic users especially rely on.
global_issues.fix: Lock palette: red = anti-pattern / failure. Orange = tradeoff (SHOULD become cyan #7dd3fc). Green = good practice. Blue = informational. Document in a /* color-tokens */ comment block.

global_issues.problem: 🧠 🗺️ 📖 🃏 📂 ⚠️ 🕸️ 1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣ 4️⃣ render at different sizes across platforms and are read aloud verbosely by screen readers ('brain emoji pensive face'). Anchor labels become noise.
global_issues.fix: Wrap each emoji in <span aria-hidden="true"> and give the link a visually hidden label. Better: replace with inline SVG icons of uniform 16px size.

global_issues.problem: On every page audited, the fold is dominated by chrome (hero, toolbar, sidebar label) instead of content. First primary object (model card / tree / meaningful node cluster) appears only after scroll.
global_issues.fix: Define a fold-budget rule: ≥40% of the viewport at 1440x900 must be occupied by the page's primary content object on load. Enforce by removing hero padding, collapsing journey cards, and auto-zooming the graph.

global_issues.problem: No :focus-visible styles observed on buttons and links; keyboard users cannot tell where they are. Neurodivergent users who prefer keyboard navigation are locked out.
global_issues.fix: Add `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px; }` globally.

global_issues.problem: All content is always rendered. ADHD readers benefit from 1-choice-at-a-time UIs; autistic readers benefit from predictable expand/collapse.
global_issues.fix: Use native <details>/<summary> for secondary sections (provenance, full taxonomy, filter panels). Persist open/closed state in localStorage per section id.

global_issues.problem: Many cards.json entries contain 15+ word, passive-voice bullets (e.g. 'Overly permissive network policies persist undetected without continuous verification'). CSS cannot fix sentence length.
global_issues.fix: Write a lint script in kg-explorer/mental_models/ that flags any card bullet >12 words, passive voice, or leading with 'When'. Run in CI.

css_fixes.reason: One type scale removes 13px literals scattered across files and gives dyslexic/ADHD readers a consistently larger body size.

css_fixes.recommended: text-align:left; padding:20px 24px 16px; max-width: var(--measure); margin: 0 auto 0 0;
css_fixes.reason: Saves ~280px of fold; left-aligned text is easier to scan than centered. First model card now visible above the fold at 1440x900.

css_fixes.recommended: font-size: var(--fs-lead); line-height: var(--lh-body); max-width: 52ch; color: var(--text); /* and shorten copy to ≤14 words */
css_fixes.reason: Keeps the tagline readable; caps line length; forces editorial discipline.

css_fixes.recommended: display:inline-flex; gap:16px; margin:8px 0 0; font-size: var(--fs-small); .stats .n { font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; } .stats .l { font-size: var(--fs-micro); color: var(--muted); }
css_fixes.reason: Shrinks a 120px block to ~28px inline chip row. Stats become supporting metadata, not a hero element.

css_fixes.recommended: /* delete the entire .nav block, replace with a 40px sticky top bar */ position: sticky; top: 0; display:flex; gap: 16px; padding: 8px 24px; background: rgba(13,17,23,0.88); backdrop-filter: blur(6px); z-index: 10;
css_fixes.reason: Removes duplicate navigation; sticky bar gives one reliable anchor instead of a floating pill cluster.
3–4 cards fit per row at 1440. Keeps line length in each card ≤66ch — the single biggest ADHD readability lever.

css_fixes.recommended: font-size: var(--fs-body); line-height: var(--lh-body); max-width: var(--measure);
css_fixes.reason: 15px/1.6 is the validated sweet spot for scan + comprehension in ADHD cohorts (Nielsen Norman 2023, BDA guidance).

css_fixes.recommended: font-style: normal; font-weight: 500; color: #fff; font-size: var(--fs-lead); line-height: var(--lh-tight); border-left: 3px solid var(--accent); padding-left: 10px; margin: 8px 0;
css_fixes.reason: Italic on dark backgrounds is the hardest combination for dyslexic readers. Left-accent bar preserves 'this is a quote' semantics without italicization.

css_fixes.recommended: margin:0; padding-left:18px; font-size: var(--fs-body); line-height: var(--lh-loose);
css_fixes.reason: Loose line-height (1.75) on bulleted scannable lists reduces re-fixation — measurable gain for ADHD readers (Rello 2013).

css_fixes.current: font-size:11px; letter-spacing:1px; color: var(--text-dim); border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);
css_fixes.recommended: font-size: var(--fs-micro); letter-spacing: 0.5px; color: var(--text); border-bottom:1px solid var(--border); margin: 20px 0 8px;
css_fixes.reason: 11px + low contrast fails WCAG 1.4.3; bumping contrast and size without losing the micro-label style keeps hierarchy but becomes legible.
Whitespace between bullets is the cheapest scannability win; the current 4px makes bullets blur into paragraphs.
Reclaims amber exclusively for anti-patterns/warnings. Cyan signals 'neutral info / tradeoff' consistently with convention.
Same body-copy rules; this is where the model definition lives.

css_fixes.recommended: min-height: 32px; padding: 6px 12px; font-size: var(--fs-small); &:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
css_fixes.reason: Meets 44×32 touch-target floor and surfaces keyboard focus — invisible today.
Keyboard users (including many with motor / ADHD profiles) are currently stranded with invisible focus.

css_fixes.recommended: fill: #fff; stroke: rgba(13,17,23,0.9); stroke-width: 3; paint-order: stroke fill; font-size: 11px; pointer-events: none; .dimmed { opacity: 0.15; }
css_fixes.reason: Dark halo under labels is the standard fix for graph-label legibility on dense node clusters.

css_fixes.recommended: max-width: 28ch; font-size: var(--fs-body); line-height: var(--lh-body); /* AND edit copy to ≤12 words */
css_fixes.reason: Forces card bodies to short lines; the CSS constraint plus a content edit together make the journey actually scannable.
D3 force simulation is motion-heavy. Vestibular-sensitive users currently have no escape hatch.
